A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same E-GRPO study. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison; v2 retains the original material and adds Appendices E–J.

before.justification: V1 reports original SFT, GRPO and E-GRPO evaluations in Tables 1–2, entity-matching analyses, training dynamics and reward-weight ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds experiments on decaying reward weights, extended training and robust entity matching, alongside failure-case analysis.

M1.justification: The core E-GRPO procedure remains unchanged. Appendix H adds an implemented robust-matching variant: an LLM generates 5–10 alternatives per entity, and matching any alternative earns entity credit. This changes reward computation in an additional training experiment.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic training sources, seven QA benchmarks, four deep-research benchmarks and Local/Web environments. The added analyses use retained coverage; entity-name expansion changes matching rather than introducing a new task or test population.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain the same SFT/GRPO comparisons and named reference-agent sets. Relabeling other baselines as reference agents does not change membership. The new appendix comparisons concern internal E-GRPO variants.

E3.justification: New Appendix F tests a 30B model with alpha declining from 0.3 to zero during the first 60 of 80 training steps. Appendix G extends Web training from 80 to 120 steps. These are additional experimental settings; the original benchmark protocols and Appendix C defaults remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 substantially expands analysis beyond the retained weight sweep and thought-versus-trajectory matching comparison. Appendices E–H add three failure-mode case studies, fixed-versus-decaying reward weights, longer-horizon training comparisons, and matching robustness analyses with an additional RL experiment.

E5.justification: The eight-rollout correlation analysis and three-rollout evaluation reporting remain unchanged. Appendix I explains the existing averaging procedure; v2 adds no independent-run counts, random-seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 retain their numerical results. New Table 3 reports mixed effects from weight decay; Table 4 reports robust-matching scores of 49.2/12.9/26.8/47.0 versus 48.5/12.9/26.4/46.7 for exact matching on GAIA/BrowseComp/BrowseComp-ZH/xbench-DS. Figures 6–7 and failure cases add supplementary findings, rather than revise the original models' scores.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6, including entity-rate normalization, advantages, rewards and the optimization objective, retain their mathematical content. Appendix I supplies a worked averaging example for the existing analysis, without adding a theorem, proof or substantive mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims: synthetic entities provide useful supervision, E-GRPO learns from near misses, and it improves accuracy and tool-call efficiency over GRPO. The appendix additions support or qualify these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: V2 substantially expands discussion of failure mechanisms and applicability limits. Appendix E distinguishes broken reasoning coherence, distracted querying and information overload, proposing topical continuity as a benefit of entity rewards. Appendix H acknowledges spelling and paraphrase limitations of exact matching, while Appendix F discusses the lack of consistent benefit from weight decay.

D1.justification: Appendix H provides the entity-variation generation prompt, candidate count and matching rule; Appendices F–G document the added schedules and training horizons. Section 4.1 also clarifies that both synthesis pipelines use Wikipedia entities. Original Appendix C hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds the Gemini 2.5 Pro reference for its writing-assistance disclosure. The substantive related-work discussion, existing cited research and claimed novelty relative to earlier search-agent training methods remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The main prose and section sequence are largely retained. V2 adds appendix cross-references, a worked explanation of Figure 1, acknowledgments and an LLM-use disclosure, and updates authorship and affiliations. These are localized editorial and structural additions rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: V2 replaces the branded report presentation with the ICLR template throughout, changing the title block, abstract treatment, headings, typography, spacing and float placement. It also adds Tables 3–4, Figures 6–7 and boxed failure examples and a prompt; the original tables and figures are retained and reflowed.

improvement.justification: Appendices E–H modestly strengthen the paper by examining failure modes, testing reward scheduling and longer training, and addressing exact matching's sensitivity to language variation. These additions provide useful evidence and clearer limitations beyond v1. The main results remain unchanged, and the small new variant gains lack additional uncertainty reporting, limiting the strength of the improvement.
